Chorus.what: The Chorus recalls the eagle omen and Agamemnon's sacrifice of Iphigenia at Aulis.
The Chorus voices dread as Cassandra raves in prophecy and goes in to die.
The Chorus argues helplessly over what to do as Agamemnon cries out within.
The Chorus prays for Orestes, exults in justice, then laments the third storm on the house.
The Furies warn that acquitting Orestes will destroy all respect for justice.
The Furies, persuaded by Athena's promises, let their anger go and agree to bless Athens.

Zeus.what: Zeus's storm engulfs Prometheus and the Chorus after Prometheus refuses to reveal his secret.

Apollo.what: Apollo promises Orestes protection and sends him with Hermes to Athens.
Apollo drives the Furies from his shrine and argues with them over matricide.
Apollo defends Orestes, claiming Zeus's command and arguing the father is the true parent.
Apollo urges a fair count as Orestes is acquitted.

Clytaemestra.what: Clytaemestra tells the Elders Troy has fallen, describing the chain of beacons.
Clytaemestra persuades Agamemnon to walk on purple tapestries into the palace.
Clytaemestra boasts of the murder, justifying it by Iphigenia's sacrifice.
Clytaemestra defends the killing and calms the quarrel between Aegisthus and the Chorus.
Clytaemestra pleads for her life and is driven inside by Orestes to die.
Clytaemestra's ghost rouses the sleeping Furies to hunt Orestes.

Orestes.what: Orestes arrives at his father's tomb, leaves a lock of hair and hides.
Orestes reveals himself to Electra and resolves on vengeance by Apollo's oracle.
Orestes reads Clytemnestra's serpent dream as his own fate and plans his disguise.
Disguised as a stranger, Orestes tells Clytaemestra that Orestes is dead.
Orestes kills Aegisthus and his mother, then flees the Furies.
Orestes clings to Athena's image and tells his case to Athena.
Orestes is acquitted, thanks Athena and Apollo, and swears Argos will never attack Athens.

Hermes.what: Hermes is charged by Apollo to guide Orestes to Athens.
Hermes demands Prometheus's secret and threatens worse torment when he refuses.

Agamemnon.what: Agamemnon arrives in triumph and yields to walking on the purple tapestries.
Agamemnon is heard crying out as he is struck down inside the palace.

Athena.what: Athena questions both sides and resolves to appoint sworn judges for a lasting court.
Athena founds the Areopagus and presides over the trial.
Athena casts the deciding vote for Orestes and begins calming the Furies.
Athena patiently persuades the Furies with promises of honour and a home.
Athena leads the Furies in a torchlit procession to their new home.

Aegisthus.what: Aegisthus explains Atreus' wrong to Thyestes, claims the murder and threatens the Chorus.
Aegisthus arrives doubtful and goes in to question the strangers.
Aegisthus is killed offstage by Orestes.

Danaüs.what: Danaüs sees an armed host approaching and tells his daughters to sit at the altar.
Danaüs reports the Argive vote and sights the Egyptian ships.
Danaus urges gratitude to the Argives and warns his daughters to guard their chastity.

Io.what: Io arrives horned and gad-fly-driven, tells her story and hears her wanderings foretold.

Cassandra.what: Cassandra raves in prophecy, foretells Agamemnon's murder and her own, and goes in to die.

Darius.what: Darius's ghost is summoned, blames Xerxes' hubris, foretells Plataea and warns against invading Greece.

Eteocles.what: Eteocles rallies the Thebans, hears the Scout and prays to spare the city.
Eteocles scolds the frightened women and goes to post defenders at the gates.
Eteocles resolves to fight his brother Polynices at the seventh gate despite the Chorus.

King.what: Pelasgus hears the maidens' Argive descent but refuses to decide without his people.
Pelasgus yields to the maidens' threat and agrees to protect them.
The King rebukes the Egyptian Herald and refuses to surrender the maidens.

Messenger.what: The Messenger reports the destruction of the Persian fleet at Salamis and the ruinous retreat.

Prometheus.what: Prometheus is nailed to the crag, laments, and tells how he saved mankind.
Prometheus lists his gifts to mankind and refuses to reveal his secret.
Prometheus foretells Io's wanderings and the hero descended from her who will free him.
Prometheus defies Hermes and is engulfed by Zeus's storm.

Pylades.what: Pylades urges Orestes to obey Loxias' oracle and kill his mother.

Xerxes.what: Xerxes returns in tattered robes and joins the Chorus in lament for the fleet.

Atossa.what: Atossa confesses her fear and tells of her dream and the eagle omen.
Atossa hears of Salamis, realises the dream was true and goes to make offerings.
Atossa brings offerings and summons Darius's ghost, then fetches clothes for Xerxes.

Electra.what: Electra, unsure how to pray, takes the women's advice and prays for Orestes and vengeance.
Electra finds the lock of hair and footprints and is reunited with Orestes.

Hephaestus.what: Hephaestus reluctantly nails Prometheus to the crag.

Herald.what: The Herald announces Agamemnon's return and reports the storm that scattered the fleet.

Antigone.what: Antigone laments her brothers and vows to bury Polynices despite the decree.

Ismene.what: Ismene joins Antigone in lamenting over her brothers' bodies.

Oceanus.what: Oceanus offers to plead with Zeus, but Prometheus refuses and he departs.

Servant.what: The servant announces Aegisthus' death and raises the alarm.

Amphiaraüs.what: Amphiaraüs, the righteous seer, is forced to fight among the Argives and is assigned a Theban opponent.

Capaneus.what: Capaneus, the giant Argive, defies Zeus and is matched against Polyphontes.

Chorus of the Processional Escort.what: The escort chorus sings the Furies to their new home beneath the earth.

Cilissa.what: Cilissa laments Orestes' supposed death and is persuaded to tell Aegisthus to come alone.

Eteoclus.what: Eteoclus attacks the Neïstan gate and is assigned a Theban defender.

Force.what: Force silently attends Power as Prometheus is bound to the rock.

Handmaidens.what: The Handmaidens join the Danaids in singing to the gods and praying against marriage.

Hippomedon.what: Hippomedon, huge Argive bearing a Typhon shield, attacks a gate and is assigned a defender.

Hyperbius.what: Hyperbius, son of Oenops, is assigned to defend against an Argive champion.

Lasthenes.what: Lasthenes is assigned by Eteocles to defend against Amphiaraüs.

Leader of the First Half-Chorus.what: The First Half-Chorus leader speaks for half the Chorus during the gate assignments.

Leader of the Second Half-Chorus.what: The Second Half-Chorus leader speaks for the other half of the Chorus.

Megareus.what: Megareus, son of Creon, is assigned as a Theban defender at a gate.

Melanippus.what: Melanippus is assigned to meet Tydeus at his gate.

Parthenopaeus.what: Parthenopaeus, youthful Arcadian with a Sphinx shield, attacks a gate and is matched with a defender.

Polyphontes.what: Polyphontes is assigned to defend against Capaneus.

Power.what: Power urges Hephaestus to rivet Prometheus to the rock, mocks him and leaves.

Prophetess.what: The Prophetess prays to the gods of Delphi, enters the shrine and returns terrified by the suppliant and Furies.

Tydeus.what: Tydeus, boastful Argive at the Proetid gate, is matched against Melanippus.

Watchman.what: The Watchman sees the beacon from Troy and hails it, hinting at troubles in the house.
